name: Bourbon Alexander
description: An Alexander you can make tonight: bourbon, crème de cacao, and Baileys in place of cognac and cream.
history: The Alexander family starts as a gin or brandy cream drink from the early 20th century. This house version keeps the chocolate-and-cream shape and uses the whiskey already on the bar.
whyItWorks: Bourbon’s vanilla and oak sit naturally under chocolate; Irish cream supplies the dairy texture the classic gets from heavy cream.
steps: Shake bourbon, crème de cacao, and Baileys hard with ice.
techniqueNotes: Eagle Rare or Penelope Architect stay polite under chocolate; a cask-strength pour will dominate.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Softer fruit and vanilla under cacao.
Polished oak for a dessert Old Fashioned energy.

substitutions.notes: Cognac is the Brandy Alexander; rye is drier and spicier.
